sentence: This project teaches researchers, ethicists and regulators how to evaluate health research that uses artificial intelligence and health biotechnologies in ethical ways.
This project studies the brain mechanisms behind lightness constancy, a form of perceptual constancy in which the brain recovers real-world variables from sensory input.
This project tests whether a predictive model and clinical decision support tool built on nurses' concerns is fair and works across health systems.
This project works with communities to reduce the burden of cancer in the county through outreach, education and partnerships.
This project tests a mechanism that could help melanoma respond better to immune checkpoint inhibitors.
This project studies how aging of brain tissue relates to how severe aphasia is and how well people recover after a stroke.
This project builds a software system that uses AI models to analyze single cells that are not fluorescently labelled.
This project tests whether inhibitors of Jumonji demethylases kill small cell lung cancer cells in models and studies how they act on the epigenome.
This project studies how a recombinant poliovirus treatment works against glioblastoma and the immune infiltrate around it.
This project designs and pilot-tests a technology-driven system that helps home healthcare nurses improve the quality of their documentation.
This project develops small-molecule compounds for brain imaging that bind a protein in microglia, to study neuroinflammation in Alzheimer's disease.
This project builds an online resource that gathers and curates genomic and biological data from Xenopus research.
This project develops a microfluidic chip method to make ready-to-inject radiopharmaceuticals on demand at low cost.
This project studies how chromosomal abnormalities called aneuploidy relate to cellular fragmentation in mammalian embryos, using comparative genomics.
This project uses dynamic light scattering to measure particle size, zeta potential and particle concentration of a lead formulation.
This project tries to improve the delivery of therapeutic polypeptides by fusing them at nonterminal sites within albumin.
This project builds a database of Veterans with colorectal cancer and links it to genetic data to create a tool that estimates individual cancer risk.
This project studies how the auditory system works and how to treat hearing problems using tools from neuroscience and neurotechnology.
This project studies what makes chimeric antigen receptor T cells work well and uses gene editing to improve them against blood and lymph node cancers.
